surface_mechanism_description: The surface reactions involve the interaction of HfCl4 and SiCl4 with surface hydroxyl groups (-OH), leading to the formation of O-Si bonds and the incorporation of silicon into the Hf–Si–O films. The reactivity of SiCl4 is different from HfCl4 towards the same reactive surface sites, with SiCl4 reacting with certain -OH groups to form O-Si bonds, while HfCl4 reacts with -OH groups to form O-Hf bonds. The bonding mode of -OH groups (isolated vs. hydrogen-bonded) influences the reactivity of SiCl4 and HfCl4.
evidence: The text states: 'The reactivity of SiCl4 is different from the reactivity of HfCl4 toward the same reactive surface sites. ... SiCl4 can react with certain –OH groups, likely formed by HfCl4 hydrolysis. ... The suggested way of reactions of SiCl4 or HfCl4 with isolated –Si–OH or –Hf–OH groups is illustrated in Fig. 4a. ... Hydrogen and oxygen are fully coordinated and, therefore, a bond with Cl from incoming SiCl4 or HfCl4 molecule could not be formed. ... Hf–Si–O growth is supported by well-separated –OH groups produced by HfCl4 hydrolysis. ... It is likely that incorporation of Si in Hf–Si–O is facilitated by –Hf–OH groups, which are more acidic than –Si–OH groups, and could promote reaction of SiCl4 with oxygen of the –Hf–OH site.'
